body.p: Claims 1-20 were pending in the present application prior to this Amendment. In this Amendment, claims 1-4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14, 15, and 18-20 are amended and claims 5, 8, and 13 are canceled without prejudice, and without waiver, surrender, or disclaimer of any argument in favor of the patentability of the subject matter recited in the claims prior to this Amendment. Claims 21-23 are added without introducing new matter to the application. Upon entering these amendments, claims 1-4, 6, 7, 9-12, and 14-23 will be pending. No claim fees are due. It is respectfully submitted that the pending claims define allowable subject matter.

Claims 14 and 18-20 were rejected as indefinite. Applicant has amended claims 14, 18, and 20 accordingly to fix the errors. Applicant requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the indefiniteness rejections upon review of the claim amendments.
Claims 1-4, 8, 10-13, 16, 18, and 19 were rejected as anticipated by Imran (US Patent 5,465,717). Applicant respectfully traverses.
Independent claim 1 recites a method that includes, in part:
obtaining a core, the core having an elongate, tubular shape;
disposing a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly relative to the core
so that at least a portion of the PCB assembly is beyond a distal end of the core, the PCB assembly including a PCB substrate and an electronic
component disposed on the PCB substrate;
coupling the PCB substrate to the core;
applying an outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly so
that a first portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along a distal segment of the core at the distal end and a second portion of the outer
sheath surrounds and extends along the PCB substrate.

Thus, claim 1 recites that at least a portion of the PCB assembly is beyond a distal end of the core, and the outer sheath is applied so that a first portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along a distal segment of the core at the distal end and a second portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along the PCB substrate. Support for this subject matter can be found in the pending application at least in Figures 2, 3, 8D, and 8E, as well as paragraphs 57, 59, 60, 69, and 70.

A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference."1 "The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in ... the claim."2 "[lI]t is not enough that the prior art reference discloses part of the claimed invention, which an ordinary artisan might supplement to make the whole, or that it includes multiple, distinct teachings that the artisan might somehow combine to achieve the claimed invention."3

The Imran reference does not describe each and every element shown in as complete detail as is contained in claim 1. For example, Imran does not describe "disposing a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly relative to the core [that has an elongate, tubular shape] so that at least a portion of the PCB assembly is beyond a distal end of the core" and "applying an outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly so that a first portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along a distal segment of the core at the distal end and a second portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along the PCB substrate."

Imran describes a mapping catheter 51 that includes a shaft 52 and an electrode assembly or basket 61 that can be advanced beyond a distal extremity 54 of the shaft 52 (Fig. 3). The electrode assembly 61 includes multiple arms 62 that are spaced apart and have an outwardly bowed shape memory. The arms 62 are connected at the shaft 52 and at a distal hub 66. Figure 5 shows a cross-sectional view of one of the arms 62. The arm

62 includes flex-circuit strip 71 secured to an elastic band or member 72. The flex-circuit strip 71 includes conductors 69 electrically connected to electrodes 68 on the outer surface of the arm 62. A heat-shrink tube 73 on the arm 62 surrounds the flex-circuit strip 71 and the elastic band 72.

The Office Action relies on the heat-shrink tube 73 as the recited outer sheath, the flex-circuit strip 71 as the recited PCB assembly, and the elastic band 72 as the recited core. But, the elastic band 72 does not have a tubular shape. Furthermore, the flex-circuit strip 71 is not disposed relative to the elastic band 72 so that at least a portion of the flex- circuit strip 71 is beyond a distal end of the elastic band 72. In addition, the tube 73 is not applied so that a first portion of the tube 73 surrounds and extends along a distal segment of the elastic band 72 at the distal end and a second portion of the tube 73 surrounds and extends along the flex-circuit strip 71. For at least these reasons, Imran does not anticipate claim 1.

In an alternate interpretation, the Office Action states that the shaft 52 of Imran can be interpreted as representing the recited core of claim 1 (OA at page 7). Although the shaft 52 has an elongate, tubular shape, and the flex-circuit strip 71 does extend beyond the distal end 54 of the shaft 52, Imran still does not describe each and every limitation and element of claim 1. For example, the heat-shrink tube 73 is a part of each individual arm 62. The tube 73 is not applied about the shaft 52 so that a first portion of the tube 73 surrounds and extends along a distal segment of the shaft 52 at the distal end 54.
Independent claim 18 recites some similar subject matter as claim 1 and is submitted to be allowable over Imran for at least the reasons described above with respect to claim 1.
Independent claims 1-20 were rejected as obvious over Imran in view of Basu.

With reference to claim 1, the secondary reference Basu does not remedy the described shortcomings of Imran. For example, no portion of the flexible electrode panel 80 is beyond the distal end of the non-conductive covering 44 of the spine 42, and there

is no outer sheath that is applied so that a first portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along the non-conductive covering 44 and a second portion of the outer sheath surrounds and extends along the flexible electrode panel 80.
Independent claim 18 recites similar subject matter as claim 1 and is submitted to be allowable over Imran and Basu for the same reasons as claim 1.
Independent claim 20 recites a method that includes, in part:
mounting a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly onto a distal

segment of the core, the PCB assembly including a PCB substrate and an electronic component disposed on the PCB substrate, the PCB substrate having a rigid or semi-rigid preformed ring shape and including a split, wherein the PCB assembly is mounted to the core by pressing the core
through the split in the PCB substrate;

Support for this subject matter can be found at least in paragraphs 57 and 63 and Figure 6A of the pending application. The cited references Imran and Basu do not teach or suggest mounting a PCB assembly onto a tubular-shaped core, where the PCB assembly includes a substrate that has a rigid or semi-rigid preformed ring shape and includes a split. For at least this reason, claim 20 is submitted to be allowable over Imran and Basu.

The dependent claims 2-4, 6, 7, 9-12, 14-17, 19, and 21-23 depend from claims 1, 18, and 20 and are allowable over the cited references based at least on the dependency from claims 1, 18, and 20. Furthermore, at least some of the dependent claims recite subject matter that is not taught or suggested by the cited references.

The pending claims are believed to be in condition for allowance. Should anything remain to place the present application in condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney at the telephone number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
